integrity_note: Every anchor row is transcribed from the checked-in research/ corpus of the Trinity repository. Aggregates below are computed by paper/data/corpus.py from the anchors array alone; the self-check asserts equality between recomputed values and the aggregates block and exits non-zero on any disagreement. No aggregate in the paper may be hand-edited here. The self-check verifies arithmetic consistency only; it cannot validate the selection of anchors or their theme assignments, which are editorial inputs. Each anchor also carries the source class it was admitted under and the content digest recorded in the matching research/ manifest; the self-check asserts the two agree and exits non-zero on any disagreement.
selection_note: This corpus is a curated motivating reading list assembled while the standard was being designed, not a survey sample. The themes were co-constructed with the paper's principles, so theme-to-principle alignment is a design fact, not independent evidence. Inclusion criterion: papers judged directly relevant to the epistemics of benchmark difficulty by the authors during drafting. Reconciliation rule: the anchors array mirrors the checked-in research/ corpus one row per .md and .pdf pair, normalized by arXiv identifier, so an on-disk paper absent from this artifact or an anchor absent from disk is a reconcile defect; the 1.1.0 round added the one on-disk paper (2606.19149) the 1.0.0 round had omitted.
